name: Art Deco faience facade
summary: Glazed terracotta slabs in bright colours and gold that clad cinemas, shops and towers of the 1920s and 1930s. The ornament is flat and geometric: zigzags, sunbursts and stepped lines.

philosophy.core_thesis: A glazed, washable slab turns a commercial building into a bright sign: colour and geometry attract the eye from the street.
design_principles: Clad the whole front with glazed slabs in one or two strong colours, with a gold or black band.
Mould the ornament in low relief: zigzags, sunbursts, chevrons, fountains and stepped forms.
Keep the slab flat, with a tight joint of 3 to 5 mm and a straight line of the grid.
Use a high-gloss or satin glaze that washes clean in the rain and in the street dirt.
Make the slab hollow and 30 to 60 mm thick, with a tie for the steel frame.
Light the facade at night; the glaze must reflect the light.
Place the tallest ornament over the entrance and at the top of the building.
anti_patterns: A deep, Victorian relief with moulded leaves
A curved, floral Art Nouveau ornament
A grey, dark wall with no colour

form.shape: Flat slabs for facades, shop fronts, cinemas and towers; piers with stepped caps, fountains and sunburst panels, with bands of relief ornament.
form.profile: A flat face with a low relief of 5 to 15 mm; the building steps back in tiers and the slab edge is sharp.
form.foot_and_rim: Each slab has a square, glazed edge and a ribbed back with a tie; a shop-front base has a thick, polished sill of black.
form.proportion: A slab is about 30 to 60 cm wide and 3 to 6 cm thick; a typical cinema front is 10 to 20 m wide and 6 to 12 m high.
rules: Use one bright colour with black and gold.
Mould zigzag and sunburst in low relief.
Make the slab hollow with a tie to the frame.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, even terracotta or a faience body that fires dense and light-coloured, so that the thin glaze shows a pure bright colour.

methods: firing of glaze and body together
forming.joins: Slabs are hung on a steel or concrete frame with metal ties and set in cement mortar with thin joints.
forming.details: A ribbed back with a tie slot, a number or mark on the edge, and a thin line of glaze that pools at the joint.

glaze.pattern: Zigzag, sunburst, chevron and stepped lines in low relief, in cream, black, blue-green and gold; plain glazed fields between the bands.
glaze.gloss: High gloss, about 80 to 95 GU, for the main colour; the black and the gold bands are satin or gloss.
glaze.wear: The glaze washes clean and keeps its colour; some slabs craze, and a few lose a corner at a sharp edge.

palette.strategy: One strong colour per building, usually cream, blue-green or black, with gold lines and one bright accent at the entrance.

firing.kiln: A large tunnel or downdraught kiln of a terracotta works; slabs stand on edge on setters in saggars.
processes: pressing or casting of the slab
a glaze firing at about 1050 to 1100 °C
hand gilding and a low-heat firing of the gold
firing.scale: A few large works in New York and on the west coast supplied cinemas, shops and towers; a tower front used tens of thousands of slabs.
firing.signs: A ribbed back, a thin glaze line at the joint and a bright, even gloss that mirrors the street.

pieces.form: Flat blue-green slab with a thin gold line for a tower front
Cream slab with a low zigzag band for a cinema front
Sunburst panel over an entrance in gold and black
Stepped pier cap in black glaze with a gold edge

positive: cream slab with a zigzag band
gold line on a black base
street photograph at dusk with lit facade

emotion.target_response: Glamour and speed: the viewer sees a bright, lit front that promises a show, a shop or a modern office.

use_cases: a render of an Art Deco cinema or tower front
a conservation note on glazed terracotta slabs
a facade pattern with zigzag and sunburst in relief
avoid_when: the brief needs a deep Victorian relief
the brief needs a matt, earth-coloured wall
the brief needs a curved, floral line

modifiers.request: early skyscraper, pale and plant ornament
modifiers.how: Change to a cream glaze, flat wall, and low plant ornament over the piers.
Remove the gloss and the ornament, use extruded panels with a matt face on rails with an air gap.

ornament_level.note: Geometry carries the ornament; keep the relief flat.

wall_thickness.note: A hollow slab is 20 to 40 mm thick at the face; the webs behind it are not counted.
